$comment: Vendored snapshot of React Native's accessibility API surface, used by
scripts/test.mjs to reject prop and API names the agents invent.
Why this exists: v1.4.0 shipped `accessibilityInvalid` in the accessibility
agent. It is not a React Native prop and never has been. 734 tests passed,
because every guard we had checked *claims* ('Reanimated 4 supports Paper')
and none checked *identifiers*. A reader on Reddit found it before any test
did. Guessing a plausible-looking prop name is the single most damaging
thing an agent of this kind can do, so it is now mechanically impossible to
Refresh deliberately when the React Native floor moves — see the
'how_to_refresh' key. Do not add a name here to silence a failure; if the
name is not in the sources below, the agent is wrong, not the snapshot.
how_to_refresh: Fetch the three files above for the new version, diff against this snapshot, and update rn_version and captured_on. Additions are usually safe; removals mean an agent may now be documenting something that no longer exists.

aria_aliases.$comment: RN 0.71+ W3C-aligned aliases. Each maps onto an accessibility* prop or accessibilityState key.

$comment: Two lists, and the difference is the point. `documented` is what
the AccessibilityRole union but is documented nowhere — every one of them
names an Android platform construct. Neither list carries a platform
annotation upstream, which is exactly why both humans and models treat all
40 as universally meaningful. They are not.

notes.flow_union_is_open: In ViewAccessibility.js the Flow AccessibilityRole union ends `| string`, so a typo such as accessibilityRole="buton" type-checks in a Flow project. The TypeScript .d.ts union has no `| string`, so TS catches it. Same prop, different safety.
notes.role_takes_precedence: reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility states that `role` has precedence over `accessibilityRole` when both are set.
notes.no_platform_annotation_on_roles: Props carry @platform ios / @platform android tags in the type definitions. Role values carry none, in either the types or the docs.
notes.set_accessibility_focus_not_deprecated: AccessibilityInfo.setAccessibilityFocus(reactTag) is present and un-deprecated in 0.87's type definitions. sendAccessibilityEvent(handle, eventType) also exists and takes a HostInstance, but the docs section covering accessibility events is titled 'Android', so its cross-platform behaviour is unverified here.
